name: Multi-Comp
purpose: Compressor with seven hardware-style modes (opto, FET, VCA, bus, studio, digital) for levelling vocals, adding punch to drums and gluing buses.

expose.ai_hint: Opto: smooth vocal levelling. Vintage FET: aggressive, forward vocals and drums. Bus: drum and mix glue. Studio modes: cleaner. Digital: precise. Set only the parameters of the chosen mode.
60-100 Hz stops low end from pumping the compressor; 0 = off.
On to keep output level matched while adjusting compression.
2x default. Off when tracking. 4x only on a final bus.
Vintage Opto only. Compression amount; 50% gives roughly 4-6 dB reduction on a typical lead vocal.
Vintage Opto only. Output gain; 50% is unity.
Vintage/Studio FET. Drive into the compressor.
Vintage/Studio FET. 4:1 for vocals; All for extreme room-mic smash only.
Vintage/Studio FET. Fast (under 1 ms) for presence; slower to keep transients.
Vintage/Studio FET. Blends raw transients past the compressor.
Classic VCA only. Upstream allows up to 120:1 (limiting); capped at 20:1 here.
Vintage VCA (Bus) only. Aim for 1-4 dB of gain reduction for glue.
Vintage VCA (Bus) only. 2:1 subtle, 4:1 classic drum glue.
Vintage VCA (Bus) only. 30ms lets drum transients punch through.
Vintage VCA (Bus) only. Auto is the classic glue setting.
Digital only. 6 dB is a soft, musical knee.

hidden_reason: Multiband mode, sidechain EQ, external sidechain, lookahead, distortion, link modes and meters stay at defaults for now; multiband needs its own catalogue entry.
notes: Starting points and hints are drawn from the Dusk Audio Multi-Comp manual (manuals/multi-comp.md).
Several thresholds and times have no unit label in code; units here follow the manual.
Each mode has its own threshold scale, so switching mode means re-setting the compression amount.
